s1.syndrome_frame: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure following a high-altitude traumatic incident with airway compromise
salient_findings: Cyanosis and tachypnoea after being buried under snow
Bilateral rales and crackles on pulmonary auscultation
Low oxygen saturation despite supplemental oxygen
key_facts: Patient was buried under snow at 2500 m above sea level
Hand remained exposed, leading to quick discovery and excavation
Patient never lost consciousness
Patient recalled being unable to breathe due to compacted snow blocking airways
Patient denied hitting any rocks or objects during burial
Initial oxygen saturation was 93% on 100% oxygen via mask
Peripheral and central cyanosis were present
Bilateral rales and crackles were heard on pulmonary auscultation
Haemoglobin levels decreased from 168 g/L to 135 g/L on day 1
CT scan showed extensive macular alveolar infiltrations throughout both lungs
No signs of trauma were noted on CT scan
Pulmonary function tests were normal 4 weeks post-incident
Echocardiography was normal 4 weeks post-incident

shortlist.label: High-altitude pulmonary edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was buried under snow at high altitude and presented with hypoxemic respiratory failure and bilateral infiltrations on CT scan

shortlist.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had hypoxemic respiratory failure, bilateral rales and crackles, and extensive alveolar infiltrations on CT scan

shortlist.label: Hypothermia-induced pulmonary edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was buried under snow and presented with hypoxemic respiratory failure and bilateral infiltrations on CT scan

shortlist.label: Aspiration pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had airway compromise due to compacted snow and presented with hypoxemic respiratory failure and bilateral infiltrations on CT scan

shortlist.label: Reperfusion injury
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a brief period of hypoxia followed by reperfusion, which could have led to lung injury and hypoxemic respiratory failure

raw.rationale: The patient was buried under snow at 2500 m above sea level, which is a high-altitude environment, and presented with symptoms such as cyanosis, tachypnoea, and bilateral rales and crackles on pulmonary auscultation, consistent with high-altitude pulmonary edema. The CT scan also showed extensive macular alveolar infiltrations throughout both lungs, which is a characteristic finding in high-altitude pulmonary edema.

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient presented with similar symptoms, the specific context of high-altitude exposure and the absence of other risk factors for ARDS make HAPE a more likely diagnosis

rejected.label: Hypothermia-induced pulmonary edema
rejected.why: There is no mention of the patient being hypothermic, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with HAPE

rejected.label: Aspiration pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient did not have any oral bleeding wounds or other signs of aspiration, and the CT scan findings are not typical of aspiration pneumonia

rejected.label: Reperfusion injury
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and CT scan findings are not consistent with reperfusion injury, and there is no mention of any ischemic event or reperfusion

gold: Negative pressure pulmonary oedema with pulmonary haemorrhage
